This one is mh_harness.dll, the determinism/replay INSTRUMENT -- seams/harness.cpp, 8.3k lines, which used to be mh.dll's single largest file. VERDICT THAT AUTHORISED IT (check_arm_order --compare, the pre-F4E run of the same mode -> the F4E run): 1 structural edit, 0 text changes, and NOTHING ELSE MOVED -- measured on all four committed templates (brokered 70->71, original 44->45, brokered_nomodule 72->73, config1 40->41). It is ONE line and not two on purpose, the same constraint both sibling binds state: the loader-order fact and the two row counts are folded into this line rather than printed separately, so the bound and absent arms are structurally identical and cost one step each. The row counts (host=27/27 spine=30/30) are the item's own evidence: host rows resolve out of mh.dll and spine rows out of libmh.dll, and `spine=0/30` is Q4's refusal stated in numbers -- configuration (1) with the instrument declining to arm rather than reading invented state. IT GOES LAST OF THE THREE BINDS, and that IS a contract (see mh.c): the instrument is handed libmh's bind verdict as an argument, so it cannot be bound before libmh has been. -- ALT (fork F4E): the same step as read on a lane with NO mh_harness.dll. Absence of the instrument is not a different ARM -- it is the same thirteen shims answering what the un-armed bodies already answered -- so it is an alternative spelling of this step rather than a fifth template. The registered `harness_absent` scenario is the lane that reads it. SECOND ALT (fork F4E): the same step on a lane where `[harness] enable=1` is set and the module is absent -- an operator who asked for an instrument and will not get one. It is a TEXT variant rather than an extra step ON PURPOSE: the refusal's own three channels (mh_harness_refused.log, OutputDebugString, stderr) carry the shouting, and a second `[modules]` line would have been a structural step that exists in one boot shape and not the others -- an unbaselined arm log for a configuration that is a mistake, which is the worst thing to make this gate argue about. Measured on workdir/mh_lanes/f4e_absent_armed. The `call-through ok` clause is not decoration and is required by tools/check_module_bind.py: GetProcAddress succeeding is not evidence that a CALL across the boundary works, and neither is the module's init returning its ABI (that is a call into the module-level entry, not into the contract). The probe is MH_Harness_WantsPresentTick, chosen for the three reasons MH_Net_IsStarted is one module over -- pure, no side effect, and a KNOWN answer at DLL_PROCESS_ATTACH (0, because load_config has not run).
